intent: These instructions explain how to calculate weekly brunch order suggestions and check them against various inventory, delivery, and supplier rules.

definitions.name: Expected Sales
definitions.text: Start from each product's average over the last four weekends. Products on offer sell about 40% more, the kit's ingredients about 10% more, and everything else about 15% more. We expect to sell about 40 kits, and each one uses a loaf, a pack of avocados and a pack of feta on top of their own sales. Round up to whole units.

constants.quote: Start from each product's average over the last four weekends.
Products on offer sell about 40% more
We expect to sell about 40 kits,

groups.quote: eggs, cherry tomatoes and rocket are on offer
a sourdough loaf, a pack of ripe avocados and a pack of feta

definitions.formula: ceil((double(record.weekend_1 + record.weekend_2 + record.weekend_3 + record.weekend_4) / double(constants.four_weekends)) * (key in groups.offer_products ? double(100 + constants.offer_increase_pct) / double(100) : (key in groups.kit_ingredients ? double(100 + constants.kit_ingredient_increase_pct) / double(100) : double(100 + constants.other_increase_pct) / double(100))) + (key in groups.kit_ingredients ? double(constants.kits_count) : double(0)))

examples.why: Average sales over 4 weekends are (28 + 31 + 30 + 31) / 4 = 30. As a kit ingredient, it sells 10% more: 30 * 1.1 = 33. Plus 40 for the kits: 33 + 40 = 73.
Average sales over 4 weekends are (19 + 21 + 20 + 20) / 4 = 20. As a product on offer, it sells 40% more: 20 * 1.4 = 28.
Average sales over 4 weekends are (3 + 3 + 3 + 3) / 4 = 3. As everything else, it sells 15% more: 3 * 1.15 = 3.45, rounded up to whole units is 4.

definitions.name: Stock Available
definitions.text: Stock available is what we have on hand, less what is reserved, plus what arrives before the start.

examples.why: Zero on hand, zero reserved, plus zero inbound before start gives zero stock available.
Fourteen on hand, less two reserved, plus zero inbound before start gives twelve stock available.
Twenty-six on hand, less zero reserved, plus twelve inbound before start gives thirty-eight stock available.
Eight on hand, less zero reserved, plus ten inbound before start gives eighteen stock available.
SD-01 case_size is 8, and proposed order is 8, which is a multiple of 8
SD-01 case_size is 8, and proposed order is 5, which is not a multiple of 8

definitions.name: Never order more than supplier can deliver
definitions.text: Never order more than the supplier can deliver.

examples.why: SD-01 proposed order is 8, max_order_units is 72, 8 <= 72 holds
SD-01 proposed order is 80, max_order_units is 72, 80 <= 72 does not hold

definitions.name: Only order what arrives before Saturday's opening
definitions.text: Only order what arrives before Saturday's opening.

examples.why: AV-RR delivery day is Friday (5), which is before Saturday (6), so it arrives before Saturday's opening
SD-01 delivery day is Saturday (6) and delivery time is 06:00 (360), which is before Saturday's opening at 07:00 (420), so it holds

definitions.name: Only order what can still be placed before the supplier's cutoff for this weekend
definitions.text: Only order what can still be placed before the supplier's cutoff for this weekend.

examples.why: SD-01 hours_until_cutoff is -3.05 (negative, past cutoff), and order is 0, so no order is placed after cutoff.
SD-01 hours_until_cutoff is -3.05 (negative, past cutoff), and order is 8 (greater than 0), so placing an order after cutoff is not allowed.

definitions.name: Aim for enough stock available
definitions.text: Aim for enough stock available to cover expected sales plus the category's safety margin.

examples.why: For SD-01, stock available is 0, expected sales is 70, safety margin is 10%, target stock is 77.0, 0 + 77 >= 77.0 is true
For SD-01, stock available is 0, expected sales is 70, safety margin is 10%, target stock is 77.0, 0 + 76 >= 77.0 is false

definitions.problem: 1 of 2 examples disagree with the formula.

definitions.name: If that isn't possible
definitions.text: If that isn't possible, flag it for a person to decide.

examples.why: Stock available 0 plus order 40 covers expected sales 33 plus safety margin 3.3
Stock available 0 plus order 0 does not cover expected sales plus safety margin

definitions.problem: 1 of 2 examples disagree with the formula.

definitions.name: Stock count age check
definitions.text: If a product's stock count is older than its category allows, flag it for a person to decide, even when nothing is ordered.

examples.why: SD-01 count age is 9.55 hours, which is less than its category max of 24 hours, so no flag is needed
AV-LS count age is 47.05 hours, which exceeds its category max of 24 hours, so a person must decide

definitions.name: Ripe avocados limit check
definitions.text: Stock available plus the order must not exceed the ripe avocados we expect to sell.

examples.why: For AV-RR, stock available is 12 and order is 0. 12 + 0 = 12, which does not exceed expected sales of 28.
For AV-RR, stock available is 12 and order is 20. 12 + 20 = 32, which exceeds expected sales of 28.
For SD-01, it is not in ripe avocados so the rule passes.

accounting.sentence: What this is for
Each week, suggest how many of each product to order for the coming Brunch weekend, so we have enough for what we expect to sell without overstocking.
A person checks and approves every order before it is placed.
The promotion
Brunch weekend runs every Saturday from 07:00 to Sunday 22:00.
The idea is to make avocado toast at home easy.
We sell an avocado toast kit (a sourdough loaf, a pack of ripe avocados and a pack of feta), and eggs, cherry tomatoes and rocket are on offer.
Ripe avocados don't keep.
How much we expect to sell
Start from each product's average over the last four weekends.
Products on offer sell about 40% more, the kit's ingredients about 10% more, and everything else about 15% more.
We expect to sell about 40 kits, and each one uses a loaf, a pack of avocados and a pack of feta on top of their own sales.
Round up to whole units.
What we have
Stock available is what we have on hand, less what is reserved, plus what arrives before the start.
Rules
Order in whole cases.
Never order more than the supplier can deliver.
Only order what arrives before Saturday's opening.
Only order what can still be placed before the supplier's cutoff for this weekend.
Aim for enough stock available to cover expected sales plus the category's safety margin.
If that isn't possible, flag it for a person to decide.
If a product's stock count is older than its category allows, flag it for a person to decide, even when nothing is ordered.
Stock available plus the order must not exceed the ripe avocados we expect to sell.
